column3: In Taiwan this is the standard word for a small rental unit with its own bathroom, typical for students and young workers; a room that shares a bathroom is 雅房. On the mainland it more often means a suite of rooms.
column4: 我在台北租了一间套房。
column5: 我在台北租了一間套房。
column6: Wǒ zài Táiběi zū le yī jiān tàofáng.
column7: I rented a small apartment with its own bathroom in Taipei.

column3: Rarely alone in speech; it turns up in 聲音, 音樂 and 口音 (accent), and for how a character is read the usual word is 讀音. It is 言, speech, with one short extra stroke added inside its mouth 口.
column6: Zhè ge zì de yīn wǒ bù huì niàn.
column7: I don't know how to say this character's sound.
